reading.title: Please Let Me Write It Down
reading.intro_zh: 这篇短文把 Lesson 48 的“嘴里有药棉、无法回答”换成一个安全的牙科沟通小误会：病人不是发现牙被拔错，而是看到自己的琴盒快被别人拿走。重点练习 when it is impossible、whether、either...or...、meanwhile 和 write down：不能说话时，怎样用手势或写字把重要信息讲清楚。
passage: On Saturday, Lily went to a dentist for a check-up before her school concert. The dentist cleaned one tooth, put cotton wool in her mouth, and told her to rest for a while. He asked whether she was ready for the concert and whether her violin case was still in the waiting room. Lily tried to answer, but she could only nod or make strange noises. Meanwhile, she was staring at the door because a little boy was walking away with a black case. At last, Lily pointed to a card on the desk and wrote, "That is my violin case." The dentist stopped, checked with the nurse, and called the boy back. Everyone laughed, but the dentist said that writing things down can be very important when a patient cannot speak clearly.

questions.question: Why could Lily not answer the dentist clearly?
options: She had forgotten all the concert music.
Her mouth had cotton wool in it after the check-up.
The nurse had asked her to leave the room.
She was too far away from the dentist to hear him.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文说 the dentist put cotton wool in her mouth，所以 Lily 不能清楚回答，不是因为忘了音乐或听不见。

questions.question: What did the dentist ask Lily about?
options: Whether she was ready for the concert and whether her violin case was still in the waiting room.
Whether she wanted to collect old match boxes after the concert.
Whether she had seen the little boy's schoolbag.
Whether the nurse had cleaned the waiting room.
questions.explanation_zh: 牙医问了两个 whether 问题：是否准备好音乐会，以及她的小提琴盒是否还在候诊室。

questions.question: How did Lily answer before she could write?
options: She sang a line from the concert.
She either nodded or made strange noises.
She called her teacher on the phone.
She left the dentist's chair at once.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文直接说 she could only nod or make strange noises，对应 Lesson 48 的 either...or...。

questions.question: What was Lily trying to tell the dentist?
options: The check-up had made her miss the concert.
The little boy was walking away with her violin case.
She wanted the dentist to clean another tooth.
The waiting room needed more chairs.
questions.explanation_zh: Meanwhile 后面说明她盯着门口，因为一个小男孩正拿着黑色琴盒走开；她写下 That is my violin case。

questions.question: Why can writing or signalling be important at a dentist?
options: It helps patients give a clear message when they cannot speak clearly.
It lets patients avoid every appointment.
It makes dentists stop asking any questions forever.
It proves that a concert is more important than a check-up.
questions.explanation_zh: 结尾说 writing things down can be very important when a patient cannot speak clearly。不能说话时，用写字或信号能把重要信息讲清楚。

writing.intro_zh: 今天抓五个 Lesson 48 的“无法回答和终于说清”句式：用 when it is impossible for you to... 写尴尬时机，用 had just...and had told... 交代之前发生的两个动作，用 tried to..., but... 写尝试被条件挡住，用 either...or... 写只能二选一的反应，最后用 At last, I was able to... 写终于能表达。

patterns.title: when it is impossible for you to ...
patterns.source: Dentists always ask questions when it is impossible for you to answer.
patterns.focus_zh: when it is impossible for you to... 用来写“偏偏在你根本不能做某事的时候”。它能制造 Lesson 48 这种尴尬又好笑的时机。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人偏偏在你无法回答、无法解释、无法离开或无法帮忙的时候问你问题。
patterns.sample: My teacher asked me a question when it was impossible for me to answer clearly.
patterns.tip_zh: 后面常接 for someone to do something：impossible for me to answer, impossible for us to leave。

patterns.title: had just ... and had told ...
patterns.source: My dentist had just pulled out one of my teeth and had told me to rest.
patterns.focus_zh: had just...and had told... 把两个更早发生的动作放在故事背景里：事情已经发生，所以现在的主角处在特殊状态。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人刚刚做完一件事，并且已经告诉另一个人做什么。
patterns.sample: The nurse had just checked my arm and had told me to sit still.
patterns.tip_zh: 两个动作都发生在后面主要情节之前，所以都可以用 had + 过去分词。

patterns.title: tried to ..., but ...
patterns.source: I tried to say something, but my mouth was full of cotton wool.
patterns.focus_zh: tried to..., but... 写“我尝试了，但条件不允许”。这个句式很适合写努力沟通却被现实挡住。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写你试图解释、回答、提醒或求助，但某个条件让你做不到。
patterns.sample: I tried to explain the problem, but my mouth was too dry.
patterns.tip_zh: but 后面要给出真正阻碍你的原因，不只是再写一个无关动作。

patterns.title: either ... or ...
patterns.source: I either nodded or made strange noises.
patterns.focus_zh: either...or... 表示“不是 A 就是 B”。这里写的是病人能做的选择非常有限：要么点头，要么发出怪声。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写你在不能正常说话、很紧张或时间很少时，只能在两个反应里选一个。
patterns.sample: I either pointed at the note or made a strange noise.
patterns.tip_zh: either 和 or 后面的结构最好保持平行：either nodded or smiled，either wrote it down or pointed to it。

patterns.title: At last, I was able to ...
patterns.source: When the dentist at last removed the cotton wool from my mouth, I was able to tell him...
patterns.focus_zh: At last, I was able to... 写“终于能够做成某事”。它适合放在故事结尾，把前面的着急变成清楚表达。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写你终于能够告诉某人一个重要信息、写下一个提醒或解释清楚一个误会。
patterns.sample: At last, I was able to write down the message for the dentist.
patterns.tip_zh: was able to 强调“终于做到了”，比 could 更适合写经过等待或阻碍后的结果。
